newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils develop advanced fraction skills by working with tenths, fractions of quantities, equivalent fractions, comparison and ordering, and fraction calculations.

This lesson includes:
✔ Using a fraction wall to compare fractions and see how equal parts change in size
✔ Reading and completing number lines in tenths
✔ Connecting tenths to decimal notation, including one tenth = 0.1
✔ Representing tenths with shapes, lengths and groups of objects
✔ Understanding that fractions must divide a whole into equal parts
✔ Finding unit fractions and non-unit fractions of quantities
✔ Using division and multiplication to find fractions such as two thirds or three quarters of a quantity
✔ Identifying and correcting common fraction mistakes
✔ Solving combined calculations involving fractions of numbers
✔ Recognising equivalent fractions using fraction walls and models
✔ Explaining equivalence, including five tenths = one half
✔ Adding and subtracting fractions, including converting to equivalent fractions where needed
✔ Ordering unit fractions and fractions with the same denominator
✔ Comparing fractions using less than, greater than and equals symbols
✔ Solving multi-step fraction problems involving measures, money, food and quantities

Pupils begin by exploring tenths on a fraction wall and number line, then connect tenths with decimals and use them in measurement and grouping contexts.

The lesson then develops fractions of quantities. Pupils use division to find one fractional part and multiplication to find several parts, before applying these strategies in increasingly challenging calculations.

Later activities focus on equivalent fractions. Pupils use models and fraction walls to identify equal values, explain why different fractions can represent the same amount, and use equivalence when adding fractions with different denominators.

The final sections develop comparison, ordering and problem solving. Pupils compare unit fractions and fractions with common denominators, choose the correct comparison symbol, and apply their understanding to multi-step questions involving measures, money and everyday contexts.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to work confidently with tenths, find fractions of quantities, recognise and use equivalent fractions, compare and order fractions, and solve addition, subtraction and problem-solving questions.
